description:
pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs:66-124 (crl_reason_serde) and the round-trip test at pkix-revocation/tests/serde_round_trip.rs:111-125 commit to: the on-the-wire form of Option<CrlReason> uses the RFC 5280 §5.3.1 numeric codes (KeyCompromise = 1, etc.).

A future contributor might suggest using the variant name strings (KeyCompromise as the JSON string "KeyCompromise") for 'readability' — they should NOT. Reasons:

1. The numeric codes are the spec's canonical identifier. RFC 5280 §5.3.1 defines them as enumerated INTEGERs with stable numeric values. The variant names are an x509-cert crate naming choice that could change across major versions.

2. Forward compatibility: from_code returns None for unrecognized values (line 94-108). A future RFC adding reason code 11 round-trips as None for current consumers without a parse error. A variant-name encoding would either fail to parse (breaking) or accept arbitrary strings (silent).

3. Interop: any external system reading the serialized form against RFC 5280 will use the numeric codes.

The hand-written deserialize_opt + serialize_opt impl IS the right shape. Do not switch to a derived serde representation.
title: Serde wire form for CrlReason uses RFC numeric codes, not variant names
